findings.statement: A lightning strike on the Eaton Socon–Wymondley circuit may have initiated the disturbance.
The order and timing of the generator trips could not be established from the work completed.
The frequency minima and the time below 49 Hz were not computed; R01 was retrieved but not analysed.
Why the ST1C speed signals disagreed and why the steam bypass pressure rose are not established.
The Hornsea de-load may relate to its control system.

report.executive_summary: Inconclusive. I could not establish the initiating event, the generation-trip sequence or the frequency landmarks with confidence from the work I completed. A lightning strike on the Eaton Socon–Wymondley circuit may have started the event [U01]. The trip sequence and the frequency figures were not determined [U02, U03]. The Little Barford root causes are recorded as not established [U04], and the Hornsea de-load may relate to its control system [U05].

sections.body: Explicitly inconclusive: see [U01, U02, U03, U04, U05].
